title: Awesome Harness project config
description: Every project-specific noun, in one validated file. If a playbook is guessing something, the fix is a new key here — never a sentence added to the core.

version.description: Core version this repository was written against. Checked at the start of every run: minor mismatch warns, major mismatch refuses. The safety belt for a single global core shared by several projects.

project.description: Short identifier for this repository. Used in reports and commit scopes.

stack.description: Preset the installer started from. Determines default conventions about file layout.

kind.description: Which tracker document in trackers/ to load. Determines how every ticket operation is performed.

board.description: Board, project or team the queue is read from. MUST be an ${ENV_VAR} reference — never a literal identifier, because this file is committed.

states.description: Maps each harness state to the literal value this tracker uses. The whole state machine is portable because of this map.

severity_order.description: Severity values from most to least urgent. The queue needs only a total order. Ties break by age, oldest first.

iteration.description: Where 'the current iteration' comes from. A cycle, a sprint, a milestone, a version in development — the playbooks only ask for the current one.

from.description: Field, relation or built-in concept holding the iteration.

current.description: Predicate identifying which one is current.

assignee.description: Who new tickets are assigned to, when the tracker models people at all. Omit when it does not.

shared.description: Whether humans also write the mapped states. When true the harness marks its own entries and ignores unmarked ones in silence.

marker_field.description: Text field the ownership marker is written into. Required whenever the board is shared.

cache_ttl.description: How long a queue read may be reused, e.g. 5m. Exists because rate-limited query APIs are common and a status check should not spend quota.

verify.description: The ordered gate. Runs in sequence; the first failure stops the task. This is the one section the installer refuses to guess — a gate that always passes is worse than no gate.

name.description: What this check is called in reports.

via.description: Non-shell invocation, e.g. an editor or tool integration. Mutually exclusive with 'run'.

require.description: Condition that counts as passing, when exit code is not enough.

scope.description: How narrowly it may run: narrowest relevant first, widening only for broad changes.

branch.description: 'current' to stay on the checked-out branch, or a pattern to derive one per ticket.

push.description: Pushing is outward-facing, so the default is the most conservative option. Anything else is a recorded authorisation.

language.description: Language commit messages are written in. Independent of the agent's reply language.

attribution.description: Whether generated work may be credited. Applies to commits and pull request bodies together — a clean history undermined by a footer is not a clean history.

commit_map.description: Change taxonomy entry to commit type. Extends the portable core for this domain. Every entry must map to exactly one type, or the field cannot decide anything.

enabled.description: Whether the ship playbook runs at all. A repository with no review culture stops at verified and committed.

granularity.description: One pull request per run. Per-ticket is intentionally not accepted: it requires a branch-per-ticket policy the execute playbook does not implement, and a key that silently does nothing is worse than an absent feature.

draft.description: Open as a draft and mark ready at the end of a clean run. Starts CI early without waking reviewers on a growing branch.

link.description: How a pull request references its tickets. A URL for trackers living elsewhere; a closing keyword for trackers native to the forge.

base.description: Base branch. Defaults to the repository's default branch.

then.description: Opening a pull request requires pushing. enabled:true with push:never is contradictory.

rules.description: Hard prohibitions specific to this repository, injected verbatim into every sub-agent prompt. The escape hatch that keeps local exceptions out of the core.

preflight.description: Conditions checked once before a run starts, each able to halt it: toolchain reachable, no conflicting editor state, expected branch, clean working tree, and — whenever pushing is enabled — that the current branch is not the default one.

artifacts.description: Where the plan playbook persists its artefacts: a path, or a named memory backend.
